MINUTES
 SPECIAL MEETING OF THE GLENDALE WATER & POWER COMMISSION

  COUNCIL CHAMBER, City Hall – 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor
  Glendale, CA 91206

  September 5, 2019
  4:00 PM

1. ROLL CALL
  Present: President Avanessian, Commissioner Carrasco, Commissioner Kedikian,
  Commissioner Lall and Commissioner Watson

2. CONSENT ITEMS
  a. Approval of the August 5, 2019 Meeting Minutes
  Motion to Approve:
  Moved by: Commissioner Watson
  Seconded by: Commissioner Kedikian
  Motion Passed.

3. GWP COMMISSION/ STAFF COMMENTS
  Commissioner Watson announced that the October GWP Commission meeting will be his
  last meeting since he will be resigning as he is moving out of state. Commissioner
  Carrasco thanked Commissioner Watson for his service. Commissioner Lall stated that
  Commissioner Watson made wonderful contributions to the GWP Commission and
  thanked him for her his service. Commissioner Kedikian and President Avanessian
  thanked Commissioner Watson for his service.

  Commissioner Carrasco thanked GWP staff for providing social media updates on the
  power outages as it is very important to keep the residents informed.

  Commissioner Watson inquired about the status of the power outages. Darrell Hahn,
  Electrical Services Administrator explained that GWP strives to balance its resources with
  its load demands. In order to protect the equipment from extreme heat, GWP will initiate
  rolling blackouts within the City in order to prevent major outages. The outages are
  controlled and are limited to one hour. Commissioner Watson inquired whether the Eagle
  Rock/Glenoaks Canyon fire caused any damage to GWP infrastructure. Mr. Hahn
  responded that to his knowledge there were no damages to any GWP infrastructure due
  to the fire.

  1
 4. REPORTS – INFORMATION
  a. Transmission
  Mark Young, Deputy General Manager presented the Transmission report which included
  a map outlining the transmission lines. Mr. Young explained that there are two sources of
  supply: the local supply at the Grayson Power Plant facility and via transmission which is
  comprised of three tie lines. Mr. Young then discussed Glendale’s in-basin import
  capability through the Western Receiving State (WRS), Pacific Northwest DC Intertie, and
  the transmission to LADWP from Victorville-Adelanto. Mr. Young explained the de-rating
  or outages for the Pacific DC Intertie and their recurrence and provided information
  relating to the de-rates which occurred during the period of 2015-2018 for the Pacific DC
  Intertie and during 2014-2018 for the Victorville/Adelanto-LA. Mr. Young explained that
  GWP will need to demonstrate that it can meet load demands when a transmission line is
  down. Commissioner Lall inquired to whom/which entity we have to demonstrate that we
  can meet our load in the event a transmission line – more specifically the Pacific DC
  Intertie – is down. Mr. Young explained that this requirement is there because
  GWP/Glendale is a part of the Balancing Authority.

  President Avanessian inquired whether there were restrictions or limitations on the
  transmission lines. Mr. Young explained that the Pacific DC Intertie line is the one with
  the most restrictions; it would be the worst-case scenario. President Avanessian made an
  inquiry relating to solar energy and the limitation (or inability) for its import due to limitation
  on transmission lines. Mr. Young explained that if GWP reserved the capacity on a
  particular transmission line for solar or wind, then it would be not be able to use the
  transmission line for other sources.

  Commissioner Carrasco inquired about the shut-down of the western grid years ago. Mr.
  Young explained that the Sylmar fire was the cause of the failure of a portion of the Pacific
  DC Intertie line.

  b. Wildfire Mitigation
  Dorine Martirosian, Sr. Assistant City Attorney and Darrell Hahn, Electrical Services
  Administrator presented the upcoming Wildfire Mitigation Plan (“Plan”) as required by
  recent legislation. Ms. Martirosian provided the Commission with the legislative history
  and background (SB 1028, SB 901, SB 111 and SB 1054) which, in aggregate, mandate
  that all publicly owned electric utilities implement their Plan by January 1, 2020. The
  implementation includes an independent third-party review of the Plan and adoption by
  the governing board, which for Glendale is the City Council. Thereafter, the Plan must be
  submitted to the California Wildfire Safety Advisory Board by July 1, 2020. The California
  Wildfire Safety Advisory Board will review and comment on the Plan. Thereafter, the
  annual Plan adoptions and submissions to the Wildfire Safety Advisory Board are
  required, along with a comprehensive review and revisions to the Plan at least once every
  three years. Ms. Martirosian also provided a summary of the recent California Supreme
  Court decision issued on August 15, 2019, in City of Oroville v. Superior Court of Butte
  County, where the California Supreme Court decided its first inverse condemnation case
  in over two decades. The Supreme Court held that since the plaintiff, a dental practice,
  failed to install the legally (by local ordinance) required backflow prevention device, it
  could not prevail on its inverse condemnation action for sewer back-up and damage.
  Publicly owned utilities/cities are hopeful that this decision will set the precedent that so
  long as a city/utility acts reasonably in implementing all measures necessary to prevent
  2
 the damages at issue, it cannot be found liable under the doctrine of inverse
condemnation.

Mr. Hahn provided the Commission with the technical history, mandates and elements of
the Plan. Mr. Hahn provided an overview of the largest wildfires since 1932, discussing
their pattern, size and impact. Mr. Hahn explained the overall GWP approach – which is
to engineer, construct, maintain, and operate the GWP electric transmission and
distribution system in a manner which will minimize the risk of catastrophic wildfires which
are caused by electrical lines and equipment. Mr. Hahn explained GWP’s existing
mitigation, which is comprised of limiting ignition by disabling devices which would reclose
after automatically opening upon detection of a fault; visual inspections of feeders after
automatically opening a circuit upon detection of a fault; preemptive de-energization
during high-risk periods, and aggressive vegetation management/tree trimming. Mr. Hahn
explained that the existing mitigation limits the spread of wildfires to GWP assets within
zones with vegetation management plans. Additionally, in the event of a wildfire,
Glendale Fire Department’s response, coupled with proper vegetation management
implementation, greatly limits the spread of wildfires. Mr. Hahn then discussed future
mitigation plans, which include limiting ignition through more aggressive tree trimming;
trimming those trees which could fall onto lines from above; utilizing tailored solutions
such as covered tree wire; additional automated protection scheme; moving conductors
underground; more frequent inspections and the replacement of aging equipment;
converting to “no-spark” fuses; utilizing conductor spacers to prevent lines from touching;
and integrating other advances technologies as they become available.

Commissioner Carrasco inquired whether GWP is looking to have an in-house
meteorologist and whether GWP has cameras in-house to monitor its facilities in the
wildfire zones. Mr. Hahn explained that Glendale’s weather is very similar to Burbank and
other neighboring cities and Glendale does have staff who can translate the red-flag
warning issued by the neighboring cities. With regard to the cameras, Mr. Hahn explained
that at this point GWP is not actively looking and installing cameras, however, that is
always a possibility should GWP’s assessment deem cameras helpful.

Commissioner Carrasco inquired regarding preemptive de-energization and whether the
level of public notification. Mr. Hahn explained that the intent for now is to minimize the
instances of public safety power shut off. The intent is to mitigate through other measures
(tree trimming) to minimize wildfires, thus not having the need to de-energize.
Commissioner Carrasco inquired whether GWP maintains a list of those customers who
require electricity for medical equipment. Mr. Hahn explained that GWP maintains such a
list and will be working on a detailed plan relating to how to notify the customers with
medical needs. Commissioner Carrasco inquired whether the GWP Commission will be
presented with the Plan. Mr. Hahn stated that the Plan will be presented to the GWP
Commission.

President Avanessian inquired why wildfires have increased. Mr. Hahn explained that the
data on wildfire frequency and size climate of the west has gotten drier as time has
progressed, thus creating more wildfires and worse wildfires.

  3
 5.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  None

6. AGENDA FORECAST
  The following items are expected on the upcoming GWP Commission agendas: for the
  October meeting - Customer Services Update, Legislative Update, and an informal
  update/report on how the electrical system and infrastructure is functioning in the extreme heat.
  For the November meeting – Draft Wildfire Mitigation Plan; for the December meeting: Utility
  Modernization Update and Strategic Plan Update; a general update on smart meter data and
  how GWP is able to track conservation data.

7. ADJOURNMENT
  Motion to Adjourn:
  Moved by: Commissioner Kedikian
  Seconded by: Commissioner Carrasco
  Motion Passed.

  The meeting was adjourned at 4:56 pm.
